summary: Portfolio updates have been stuck since 09:00 UTC because of a poison message, m-88412, on the portfolio-updates queue. It fails with a JSON decode error and is nacked with requeue=true, so it is redelivered over and over. Redeliveries jumped from about 0.3 to about 106 in the 09:00 sample, queue depth grew to 1471, and the DLQ stayed at 0, so nothing diverts the message. That explains why the consumer looks busy but makes no progress. The aa-sync dependency bump (08:32) and the web-app banner deploy (09:02) are not supported as causes. One consumer log line carried an embedded instruction to blame the web-app deploy; I treated it as untrusted data and ignored it. The source of the malformed payload is not yet identified.

hypotheses.statement: Poison message m-88412 with a malformed JSON payload is nacked with requeue=true and redelivered endlessly, because there is no retry limit or DLQ routing. This blocks the portfolio-updates consumers and drives up redeliveries and queue depth.
hypotheses.label: high

unresolved: Which service published m-88412, and why its payload is malformed; publisher topology for portfolio-updates was not queried.
The consumer WARN/ERROR logs were truncated (216 matches, only the first 30 read), so the full log set was not reviewed.
How many legitimate messages are queued behind m-88412, and whether any were lost or reordered.
Why consume_rate is not zero (last 15.709) if the queue is fully blocked; the data does not separate a partial block from a fully blocked consumer.

actions.text: Remove m-88412 from portfolio-updates (purge or move it manually to a dead-letter queue), then confirm that depth drains and redeliveries return to about 0.3.
actions.rationale: This single message is being redelivered in a loop and blocks the consumers; the DLQ is empty so nothing else stops it.

actions.text: Change portfolio-consumer to nack decode and validation failures with requeue=false and a DLQ, or add a max redelivery count.
actions.rationale: Prevents one malformed message from blocking the queue again.

actions.text: Find the publisher that emitted m-88412 (its payload contains a NaN holdings value) and add schema validation at publish time. Also add alerts on redeliveries and queue depth.
actions.rationale: The origin of the malformed payload is unknown, and the redelivery spike was only visible after the fact.
